If two entangled states can be transformed into each other but do not satisfy local unitary equivalence, then both can be decomposed into an entangled block and a separable part, and the two parts can be distinguished by local measurements. The two entangled blocks have the same probability weight and satisfy local unitary equivalence, while the separable parts may differ. We further prove that every entangled state has a unique least retained block; after retaining its probability weight, the local unitary equivalence class of this block completely determines the reversible equivalence class of the original state. For negative partial transpose states, one only needs to compute the negative spectral subspace of the partial transpose and perform at most three matrix zero tests to determine this retained block.
item.dc:creator: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong, Ming Yang

item.title: Emergent SSH physics and localization in a cavity--atom system beyond the rotating-wave approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.11897v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a cavity--atom system beyond the rotating-wave approximation and recast its dynamics as an effective tight-binding problem in the excitation-number basis. The same experimentally relevant light--matter platform exhibits two distinct regimes controlled by the photon number. In the large-photon-number regime, the hopping amplitudes become nearly uniform and the effective lattice reduces to a dimerized SSH-type chain subject to a linear energy gradient. The spectrum then organizes into one or two Wannier--Stark ladders, giving rise to controllable Bloch and Bloch--Zener oscillations and quantitatively explaining the observed revival patterns. In the small-photon-number regime, the intrinsic $\sqrt{\bar n+(\cdots)}$ dependence produces a pronounced hopping deformation, namely dimerized couplings that increase along the excitation-number lattice. This deformation reshapes the density of states, enhances collective localization, and generates an energy-resolved spatial bias of the eigenstates. The corresponding real-time dynamics displays direction-dependent anomalous diffusion together with Bloch-like revivals and beat phenomena in selected parameter windows. Our results show that the same cavity--atom platform can realize both emergent ladder spectra and hopping-induced localization in excitation-number space.
item.dc:creator: H. Shen, J. Cao, R. Wang, X. Z. Zhang

item.title: Hamiltonian-Dependent Compressibility and Physical Preservation in Approximate Quantum Compilation using Tensor Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Approximate quantum compilation (AQC) using tensor networks provides a promising route to reducing the circuit resources required for quantum simulation. However, the factors governing the compressibility of many-body dynamics and the extent to which compressed circuits retain physically relevant information on quantum hardware remain poorly understood. We investigate these questions using AQCtensor for an 80-qubit one-dimensional anisotropic XYZ Heisenberg chain initialized in a N'eel state. By varying the exchange anisotropy and external magnetic field, we find that compression performance changes systematically with the anisotropic coupling configuration and field orientation. These variations are strongly associated with a nested-commutator measure related to second-order Trotter error, with corresponding directional trends also reflected in the target-state MPS bond dimension. For an 80-qubit quantum-hardware evaluation, AQCtensor compresses a 10-repetition target evolution to 5 repetitions while retaining a target-state fidelity of 0.995474, reducing the total circuit depth by 45.9% and the two-qubit gate count by 47.6%. The compressed circuit exhibits comparable behavior across magnetization, nearest-neighbor correlation, and Hamiltonian expectation measurements, while process-level diagnostics and local reduced-state tomography provide complementary characterization beyond these observables. Together, these results link AQCtensor compressibility to Hamiltonian commutator structure and target-state complexity and demonstrate substantial circuit reduction while retaining physically relevant features in an 80-qubit quantum-hardware experiment.
item.dc:creator: Dohyun Kim, Namshik Han

item.title: V-type Atomic Variance Squeezing
item.description: arXiv:2610.18362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Variance squeezing of a V-type atom interacting with a dissipative cavity is investigated. First, the influence of atomic initial state parameters on the variance squeezing is explored. The results show that the atomic variance squeezing switches alternately between Sx and Sy as the initial state parameter alpha sweeps from -pi to pi. The two squeezing intervals are symmetric about alpha = pi/4, each with a width of pi/2. For alpha = pi/14, only the Sx component can generate variance squeezing and will eventually disappear with time evolution due to unavoidable environmental noise. Then, the influence of system parameters on the variance squeezing is also studied. It is found that, the optical variance squeezing depth of Sx is determined solely by the atomic initial parameters and is independent of the system parameters. Both weak cavity-environment coupling and atom-cavity detuning can significantly enhance the robustness of the Sx variance squeezing. The SGI parameter has an extremely weak influence on variance squeezing. These results are beneficial for high-precision quantum communication applications.
item.dc:creator: Chenrui Bi, Hong-Mei Zou, Zhao-Yang Tong, Zijin Liang

item.title: Constrained dissipation and the lifetime of quantum many-body scars
item.description: arXiv:2610.22223v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the fate of quantum many-body scars in the PXP model subject to Markovian dissipation. We show that when local jump operators respect the same symmetries of the Hamiltonian the full Liouvillian spectrum displays a tower of states with properties analogous to standard quantum scars: large overlaps with N\'eel states and equally spaced gaps in the imaginary part of the eigenvalues, set by a single frequency. Whether the long-time dynamics is dominated by scars is determined by the real parts of the eigenvalues, which are set by the ratio between the two relaxation rates $\gamma_{\pm}$ describing spin flips down-to-up or up-to-down respectively. For asymmetric dissipation ($\gamma_+ > \gamma_-$) the scarred eigenvalues have the smallest real parts: the resulting enhanced fidelity oscillations are further stabilized by staggered jump operators. In contrast, replacing the full projection operator in the dissipators with a partial one breaks the symmetries of the problem and is seen to destroy dissipative scars altogether.
item.dc:creator: Weyner Ccuiro, Rosario Fazio, Alessandro Silva

item.title: Majorization for superpositions of nonorthogonal states and the existence of golden states
item.description: arXiv:2610.26483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Golden states, from which every state can be prepared by free operations, are the units of a resource theory. In the resource theory of superposition relative to linearly independent, nonorthogonal reference states, they were known only for two reference states and for special overlap matrices, all of them maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis. We determine what decides their existence and when this L\"{o}wdin pattern holds. For every overlap matrix, the robustness and the geometric measure of superposition are maximized by the same states, which overlap equally with all reference states; the maximal values are set by the ground-state energy of a classical $XY$ model on the dual basis. These states, and only these, are golden under the maximal superposition-free operations, but they need not be maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis. For the Kraus-type free operations, we prove Gram majorization, a necessary and sufficient criterion for converting pure states into targets with nonzero coefficients, which reduces to majorization for orthonormal reference states. It shows that every golden state of these operations is maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis, yet golden states exist only for special overlap matrices: three reference states that are not orthonormal admit one if and only if their overlaps have a common modulus $s$ and their Bargmann phase $\Phi$ obeys $s\geq2\cos[(\pi+|\Phi|)/3]$, so that a geometric phase decides whether the theory has a unit. Finally, equal-overlap states yield a complete family of superposition witnesses in the L\"{o}wdin basis, which show that white noise is a resource unless the reference states are orthonormal.
item.dc:creator: G\"{o}khan Torun

item.title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26843v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). This foundational control problem often requires solving a nonlinear matrix Riccati equation, which can be costly for large systems and long control durations on conventional classical solvers. We instead work directly with the state-costate optimality equations, reformulating the LQR problem as a multiple-shooting linear system. Importantly, we prove a condition-number bound for the system that is independent of the horizon, under stabilizability and detectability assumptions. By incorporating the initial and final conditions into a single linear system, we can solve the subsequent linear system more efficiently with a quantum linear systems subroutine. For a given initial state, our quantum algorithms return classical estimates of the optimal cost and the optimal control inputs at a selected time, without constructing a Riccati solution operator. Given sparse-matrix block-encodings, an initial-state preparation oracle and a fixed number of control inputs, the query and gate complexities scale polylogarithmically with system size and control duration, provided that sparsity, relevant norms, and stability parameters are bounded. The dependence on the target error is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors. We establish the required bounds uniformly in system size and duration for a family of damped mass-spring chains with two endpoint controls. Numerical experiments support the analysis.
item.dc:creator: Xiajie Huang, Cristina \'Alvarez Yuste, Nikita Guseynov, Nana Liu, Javier Gonz\'alez-Conde

item.title: Cooling more while dissipating less: anomalous tradeoffs from thermodynamic geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.27948v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that, starting from the same state, optimal driving can sometimes reach a colder (or hotter) target in the same amount of time while dissipating less energy, or equivalently dissipate the same amount of energy in a shorter time. We study this counterintuitive phenomenon in the slow-driving regime of an open quantum system, where we name it Near-Equilibrium Anomalous Tradeoff (NEAT). We establish necessary conditions for its occurrence and show its underlying geometric origin. While NEAT is reminiscent of the well-known Mpemba effect, the two phenomena are distinct in general. We demonstrate NEAT in an exactly solvable qutrit model, as well as for d-dimensional birth-death dynamics with independently controlled energy levels. Finally, we show how NEAT can improve the performance of Carnot engines.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Canzio, Vasco Cavina, Salvatore Raia, Vito Vetrano, Matteo Scandi, Paolo Abiuso

item.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodictive tests: a unifying classical variational principle
item.description: arXiv:2610.29696v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A single classical f-divergence has several inequivalent quantum versions, but what distinguishes them operationally is less clear. Matsumoto's reverse tests characterize the maximal quantum f-divergence as the least classical distinguishability needed to prepare two quantum states with one device. Here we introduce retrodictive tests, in which two reverse tests sharing a reference state are coupled via Bayesian retrodiction to define a forward and a reverse stochastic process. In the forward process, the system is prepared by the first device and measured by the Petz transpose of the second; the reverse process interchanges their roles. We seek the least classical distinguishability between these two processes, as measured by the f-divergence between their joint laws, for fixed prescribed states and reference. For full-rank states in finite dimension, we prove that the canonical spectral implementations attain this minimum simultaneously for every operator-convex f. The reference then determines which quantum f-divergence is obtained: a flat reference gives the standard divergences, with the Nussbaum--Szko{\l}a distributions as optimal joint laws; either prescribed state as reference recovers Matsumoto's reverse tests and the maximal divergences; and power references give the geodesic family. In particular, the Umegaki and Belavkin--Staszewski relative entropies arise from the same classical variational principle under different choices of reference. Spectral optimality extends to processes containing a quantum channel; for channels with full-rank Choi operator, the minimum of the forward relative entropy agrees with a known average entropy production.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Buscemi

item.title: Elementary proofs of quantum lower bounds for element distinctness and k-sum
item.description: arXiv:2610.32693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give elementary proofs of the $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ quantum query lower bound for element distinctness and the $\Omega(n^{k/(k+1)})$ lower bound for the $k$-sum problem, for fixed $k$ and sufficiently large groups. The proofs use only basic properties of quantum states and linear algebra, analyzing the differences of algorithm states on different inputs.
item.dc:creator: Andris Ambainis, Martins Kokainis

item.title: Nonclassicality from Incomplete Fock-State Statistics
item.description: arXiv:2610.32908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nonclassicality in bosonic systems can be certified directly from occupation probabilities without full state reconstruction. To complete a library of such criteria we introduce a numerical framework that constructs optimal linear nonclassicality witnesses from arbitrary subsets of measured occupation probabilities by solving a semi-infinite linear program. The method contains known analytical criteria as special cases while generally detecting substantially larger nonclassical regions. We provide an open-source implementation of the numerical optimization together with the analytical criteria discussed here, enabling direct application of the framework to measured occupation statistics across bosonic platforms. As a case study, we apply it to the resonant Jaynes--Cummings model with thermal states and reveal nonclassicality at short interaction times and close to thermal balance, where detection of nonclassicality is otherwise challenging.
item.dc:creator: Martin \v{Z}onda, Pavel Bal\'a\v{z}, Luk\'a\v{s} Lachman, Darren W. Moore, Tom\'a\v{s} Novotn\'y, Radim Filip

item.title: Classification of the Karlsson-Szollosi Intersection
item.description: arXiv:2610.33207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that $K_6^{(2)} \cap X_6^{(2)} = D_6^{(1)} \cup C_6^{(1)}$ up to standard Hadamard equivalence, where $C_6^{(1)}$ is a non-affine one-parameter family of complex Hadamard matrices. This demonstrates that the intersection of the two-parameter Hadamard families of Karlsson and Sz\"oll\H{o}si is strictly larger than the affine Di\c{t}\u{a} curve $D_6^{(1)}$. Our new parametrisation of the Sz\"oll\H{o}si family $X_6^{(2)}$ in Karlsson coordinates and our constructive classification of the Karlsson-Sz\"oll\H{o}si intersection shed light on the intersection of block-reducible forms and hypocycloid constraints. This may support the search for mutually unbiased bases in composite dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Ranchin

item.title: Suppressing microwave crosstalk in superconducting quantum processors by designing parasitic drive capacitances
item.description: arXiv:2610.36365v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As superconducting quantum processors scale to large qubit counts, unwanted microwave drive crosstalk becomes an important source of coherent errors. Here, we investigate the role of parasitic coupling paths in the suppression of drive crosstalk in a processor with two fixed-frequency transmon qubits and a tunable coupler. To account for the many different coupling paths, we develop a detailed circuit model to capture the dependence of crosstalk on the coupler frequency. We experimentally demonstrate suppression of crosstalk, finding that the suppression does not originate solely from cancellation of the effective qubit-qubit coupling, but also is a result of interference between other coupling paths. Building on these insights, we show that drive crosstalk can be suppressed with the right choice of parasitic capacitances, which otherwise often are treated as unwanted design imperfections. Our results provide practical guidance for low-crosstalk device design of superconducting quantum processors and point toward a broader strategy in which parasitic coupling paths are engineered rather than simply minimized.
item.dc:creator: Anuj Aggarwal, Jorge Fern\'andez-Pend\'as, Simon Pettersson Fors, Zakaria Mohamed, Halld\'or Jakobsson, Amr Osman, Janka Bizn\'arov\'a, Andreas Nylander, Anita Fadavi Roudsari, Marcus Rommel, Anton Frisk Kockum, Giovanna Tancredi

item.title: Defining 2-group symmetries on lattices and extracting their anomalies
item.description: arXiv:2610.37745v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ordinary $0$-form symmetries $G$ can mix with $1$-form symmetries $\Pi_2$ to form a $2$-group $\mathcal{G}$. We give a concrete lattice definition for a class of finite $2$-group symmetries in terms of local relations among symmetry operators. These relations identify the Postnikov class $[\rho]\in H^3(BG,\Pi_2)$ that characterizes the mixing. We develop a method to extract anomalies of these symmetries in one spatial dimension by restricting symmetry operations to an interval and comparing their composition near its endpoints. We also construct explicit qubit symmetry actions in $d=1,2,3$ spatial dimensions for a $2$-group with $G=\Pi_2=\mathbb{Z}_2$. These actions share the same nontrivial Postnikov class but include both anomaly-free and anomalous realizations. Their cohomological anomalies are classified by $H^{d+2}(B\mathcal G,U(1))$, which is $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=1,2$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ for $d=3$, and our constructions realize every class in these dimensions. Our results connect higher-group symmetry and its anomalies to concrete lattice operations, providing a microscopic framework for studying anomalous symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Feng, Yu-An Chen

item.title: Coherent errors, syndrome extraction and the Robustness of Magic in stabiliser codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38554v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coherent errors leave stabiliser-code-encoded magic states in superpositions of syndrome sectors. We ask how much magic these coherent errors add, and whether syndrome extraction depletes logical magic. Using Robustness of Magic, we show that, for a unitary error U on a correctable region which supports no stabiliser, the encoded state has the same robustness as the logical state plus one copy of the Choi state of U , in every stabiliser code encoding. Syndrome extraction removes this copy, returning the logical robustness. The removed magic is positive for every non-Clifford error: adding a non-stabiliser state to any state multiplies one plus the robustness by a (tightly- bounded) factor above one. The magic capacity of two-qubit gates Clifford-equivalent to diagonal or single-qubit gates is equal to their Choi-state robustness. We give a linear-algebraic test for when a Clifford error makes syndrome extraction measure a logical operator, and give magic lifetimes of stored single-qubit magic states under Pauli noise. Choosing the plane of the stored state extends these lifetimes about 1.5x on rotated surface codes under low code-capacity depolarising noise. We identify states and channels in odd-prime dimension for which Wigner negativity and robustness show equal lifetimes.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Bozzetto, Jonte R. Hance

item.title: Local Quantum Fault Tolerance Without Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.38847v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study fault-tolerant quantum computation using a fixed, local error-correction rule and a geometrically simple code: the cubical $(d,d')$-Toric code with $d',d-d'\geq 2$, including the 4D Toric code. Under sufficiently weak local-stochastic Pauli noise, our construction uses noiseless, bounded-depth classical processing per physical time step. Its correction cycle acts only on the current syndrome, has constant depth, and is repeated unchanged during idle logical computation; it requires neither multiscale decoder states nor scale-dependent communication delays. Our proof treats errors and syndromes as chains in a cubical complex, combining geometric shrinking under the sweep rule with a space--time explanation-tree argument inspired by Toom's theorem. It does not rely on expansion. We establish three results: 1.Explicit higher-dimensional sweep rule. We give a local algorithm for choosing sweep corrections on cubical $(d,d')$-Toric complexes, resolving the local-existence question of Kubica and Preskill. 2. Fault-tolerant computation. We prove a circuit-level threshold theorem for noisy sweep cycles interleaved with logical gates. In particular, the 4D Toric code admits a fixed, constant-depth syndrome-based correction cycle without a multiscale decoder or expansion-based encoding. We do not claim constant total-depth overhead. 3. Ideal decoding under local-stochastic noise. For an initial local-stochastic Pauli error of rate $p$ below threshold, $n^{d+1}$ noiseless sweep cycles recover the encoded state on a side-length-$n$ $(d,d')$-Toric code with probability at least $1-O(\operatorname{poly}(n))p^{\Omega(n)}$, extending earlier guarantees for independent errors.
item.dc:creator: David Ponarovsky

item.title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
item.description: arXiv:2610.40561v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) variants are among the leading candidates for electronic structure calculations on quantum computers, gradient-based operator selection limits their scalability. To solve this, we introduce the Hamiltonian-gradient-free VULCAN (Variational Upbuilding, Layered Compression, Adaptive N-body perturbation) layered VQE framework. Our method dynamically generates ansatz operators using Variational Double Bracket Flow (VDBF) equations. Combined with a linearly scaling minimal complete pool, it creates a pool 4-12 times smaller than QEB (Qubit-Excitation-Based) pools. By appending entire layers simultaneously, Hamiltonian gradient measurements are completely eliminated. Circuit depth is managed via a grow-then-compress scheme using efficient state-overlap measurements, and qubit requirements are reduced by projecting the Hamiltonian onto a dominant-determinant subspace. Using high-performance emulation up to 32 logical qubits, we achieve chemical accuracy at just 5-20% of the measurement cost of batched ADAPT-VQE for hydrogen chains, BeH2 and H2O. For the 32-qubit C3H6, where batched ADAPT-VQE does not reach chemical accuracy, a single VULCAN layer combined with a GPU-accelerated stochastic Epstein-Nesbet (ENPT2) correction does. This stochastic ENPT2 post-processing step enables early termination at chemical accuracy. Discussions of hardware implementations are reported alongside an initial proof-of-principle experiment on a Quantinuum System Model H2 trapped-ion quantum processor.
item.dc:creator: Hugo D. Nogueira, Siwar Badreddine, Olivier Adjoua, Diata Traore, Guillaume Michel, Jean-Philip Piquemal

item.title: Equilibria of Replicator Dynamics in Quantum Games
item.description: arXiv:quant-ph/0106135v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyse two-population replicator dynamics for asymmetric $2\times2$ games implemented with the Marinatto--Weber (MW) identity/bit-flip protocol. The effective payoff matrices are explicit convex combinations of relabelled classical matrices. Consequently, the dynamics depends on the initial state only through its four computational-basis probabilities: quantum phases, coherences and entanglement cannot be distinguished from classical shared randomness by the payoffs or trajectories in this protocol. At each pure-strategy vertex, the local eigenvalues equal the negatives of the corresponding unilateral payoff advantages; a vertex is asymptotically stable precisely when it is a strict Nash equilibrium, and thus an evolutionarily stable strategy pair in the asymmetric-game sense. Explicit examples show how varying the initial distribution changes which vertex is stable. When an isolated interior rest point exists, it is a saddle or a nonlinear centre according to the sign of the product of the classical payoff cross-differences; the sign cannot change under the MW mapping, although the point can enter or leave the strategy square. We give all four vertex-stability conditions explicitly in a single table, obtain a closed-form logistic solution on the parity-balanced hyperplane $S=0$, classify the degenerate cases, and give a first integral for the nondegenerate flow. All results concern the MW payoff protocol and its classically simulable family of bimatrix games; none constitutes evidence of an inherently quantum evolutionary advantage.
item.dc:creator: Azhar Iqbal, A. H. Toor

item.title: IterTestQ: Assembly-Level, Cross-Platform Testing of Quantum Computing Platforms
item.description: arXiv:2503.17322v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum computing platforms are susceptible to quantum-specific bugs, such as incorrectly ordering qubits or incorrectly implementing quantum abstractions. These bugs are difficult to detect and require specialized expertise. The field faces challenges due to a fragmented landscape of platforms and rapid development cycles that often prioritize new features over thorough testing, severely hindering the reliability of quantum software. To address these challenges, we present IterTestQ, a novel cross-platform testing approach for quantum computing platforms. The key technical contribution is our novel ITE process, which generates equivalent quantum programs by iteratively (I)mporting them into platform-specific representations, (T)ransforming the program via optimizations and gate conversions, and (E)xporting the program again. To transfer programs across platforms and test cross-platform consistency, IterTestQ leverages QASM, an assembly-level representation supported by most platforms. The approach uses a crash oracle to detect failures during cross-platform transformations and an equivalence oracle to validate the semantic consistency of the generated assembly programs, which are expected to be equivalent by construction. We evaluate IterTestQ on widely-used quantum computing platforms, including Qiskit, PennyLane, Pytket, BQSKit, and Cirq, revealing 23 bugs, 17 of which are already confirmed or fixed. Our results also demonstrate that IterTestQ complements existing quantum fuzzers (covering tens of thousands of otherwise uncovered lines), is efficient (with 0.00089 seconds per generated program), and that the ITE process is crucial for its effectiveness.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Paltenghi, Michael Pradel

item.title: An integrated photonic millimeter-wave receiver with sub-ambient noise temperature
item.description: arXiv:2510.06176v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Growing demands for timing precision in positioning systems, and resolution in atmospheric sensing and automotive radar, have extended receiver frontends into the millimetre-wave and THz regimes. At these frequencies, the noise performance of field-effect transistors used in low-noise amplifiers degrades rapidly due to parasitic effects, limited carrier mobility, hot electrons, and shot noise. Parametric transducers that couple electromagnetic signals to optical fields can offer quantum-limited sensitivity at room temperature. Electro-optic materials can enable receivers that transduce radiofrequency signals into optical phase shifts. Yet to date, room-temperature receivers using electro-optical detection have not attained a noise figure comparable to the electronic amplifiers. Here we demonstrate a room-temperature cavity electro-optic-based millimetre-wave receiver on a lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuit, achieving an on-chip photon-number transduction efficiency of 10%. The equivalent input-referred receiver-added noise temperatures reach $110\,\mathrm{K}$ on-chip and $202^{+35}_{-33}\,\mathrm{K}$ for the full system at 60.5 GHz, with noise figure matching state-of-the-art V-band electronic low-noise amplifiers. We resolve the thermal noise in cavity electro-optic transducers, showing that the system is limited by thermal photon occupation ($\sim$100) in the millimetre-wave cavity and optical vacuum noise, with no measurable excess noise. Our work demonstrates that integrated photonics can reach state-of-the-art electronic receiver noise performance while offering high-radiofrequency-power survivability and compatibility with remote optical readout. This establishes cavity electro-optics as a low-noise, electromagnetic interference-resilient, chip-scale receiver frontend for millimetre-wave applications, enabling scalable analogue processing in the optical domain.
item.dc:creator: Junyin Zhang, Shuhang Zheng, Jiachen Cai, Connor Denney, Zihan Li, Yichi Zhang, Changhao Han, Xin Ou, Gabriel Santamaria-Botello, Tobias J. Kippenberg

item.title: Unlocking n-alk-1-ynes Conformers: Quantum "Trigger Finger" versus "Stiff Joint" Conformations
item.description: arXiv:2511.02470v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Molecular conformation in n-alk-1-ynes (CnA) is conventionally simplified to an all-planar structure. We report a comprehensive quantum chemical analysis revealing two near-isoenergetic rotamers at the acetylenic terminus: planar (C$_s$) and skewed (C$_1$). The high, symmetric rotational energy barrier ($\approx 150$\,meV) arises from unique steric relief near the $\mathrm{sp}$ center coupled with electronic stabilization of C$_1$. This creates a unique kinetic profile: a Quantum ``Trigger Finger'' ($\alpha$ rotation) that enforces an $\approx 50\%:\,50\%$ $\mathrm{C}_s/\mathrm{C}_1$ ensemble, sharply contrasting with the thermodynamically biased ``Stiff Joint'' ($\delta$ rotation) of the alkyl chain. This structural degeneracy necessitates ensemble averaging for spectroscopic data interpretation, while the slow interconversion permits kinetic trapping and intentional conformer enrichment during synthesis and molecular junction fabrication. Our work redefines the alkyne anchor, providing a blueprint for accurate interpretation of spectroscopic data and achieving conformational control in molecular electronics.
item.dc:creator: Ioan B\^aldea

item.title: Time Evolution of Multi-Party Entanglement Signals
item.description: arXiv:2511.16729v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the real-time dynamics of multi-party entanglement signals in chaotic quantum many-body systems including but not necessarily restricted to holographic conformal field theories. We find that scrambling dynamics generates multiparty entanglement with rich structure including: (a) qualitatively different dynamical behaviours for different signals, likely reflecting different dynamics for different kinds of entanglement patterns, (b) discontinuities indicating dynamical phase transitions in the entanglement structure, (c) transient and non-monotonic multiparty entanglement, and (d) periods during which the extensive entanglement of some regions is entirely multipartite. Our main technical tool is the membrane theory of entanglement dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Vijay Balasubramanian, Hanzhi Jiang, Simon F. Ross

item.title: Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
item.description: arXiv:2511.18512v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study neural-network approximation of density functionals in a Banach-space setting. Since the exact continuum functionals are discontinuous in the natural density topology, we apply $p$-Moreau-Yosida regularization. We construct finite-rank ReLU networks that preserve convexity and nonnegativity, lie below the regularized functional, and approximate it uniformly on compact sets. For energies obtained by minimization over compact density sets, we account exactly for the energy shift caused by regularization and bound the remaining error by the localization on these compact sets and network approximation errors. We apply this framework to canonical and grand-canonical density-functional theory at fixed particle number and fixed mean particle number, respectively. We obtain uniform energy convergence on norm-compact classes of external potentials, including molecular Coulomb potentials. We illustrate our results through numerical experiments on a simple model system.
item.dc:creator: Andre Laestadius, Mathias Oster

item.title: Momentum entanglement at colliders: the $H \to WW,ZZ$ case
item.description: arXiv:2512.02104v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We address momentum entanglement in Higgs decays to weak boson pairs, $H \to WW,ZZ$, by discretising momentum space. The momenta of the two weak bosons are entangled, as well as the degrees of freedom in momentum and spin spaces. For $H \to ZZ$ in the four-lepton final state, we also estimate the statistical sensitivity of entanglement measures at the Large Hadron Collider and future upgrades. The discretisation method introduced here is broadly applicable, offering a framework for studies of momentum entanglement at the energy frontier.
item.dc:creator: J. A. Aguilar-Saavedra

item.title: Entanglement in the Schwinger effect
item.description: arXiv:2512.10091v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze entanglement generated by the Schwinger effect using a mode-by-mode formalism for scalar and spinor QED in constant backgrounds. Starting from thermal initial states, we derive compact, closed-form results for bipartite entanglement between particle-antiparticle partners in terms of the Bogoliubov coefficients. For bosons, thermal fluctuations enhance production but suppress quantum correlations: the logarithmic negativity is nonzero only below a (mode-dependent) critical temperature $T_c$. At fixed $T$, entanglement appears only above a critical field $E_{\text{entang}}$. For fermions, we observe a qualitatively different pattern: the fermionic logarithmic negativity is non-vanishing at finite temperature, and is monotonically suppressed by thermal noise. As a function of the electric field, it is non-monotonic, featuring a temperature-independent optimal field strength $E_*$ and decreasing on both sides of the maximum. We give quantitative estimates for analog experiments, where our entanglement criteria convert directly into concrete temperature and electric field constraints. These findings identify realistic regimes where the quantum character of Schwinger physics may be tested in the laboratory.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Kranas, Amaury Marchon, Silvia Pla

item.title: Symmetry-Protected Topological Structures in Quantum Many-Body Scar Subspaces
item.description: arXiv:2512.11216v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate how symmetry-associated topological properties, originally defined for ground states, can be consistently extended to dynamically isolated subspaces of quantum many-body systems. Focusing on quantum many-body scars (QMBS), we show that a scar subspace is invariant under the relevant symmetries, and it can support well-defined topological properties inherited from an underlying symmetry-protected topological (SPT) ground state, even though individual scar states need not themselves be symmetric. We refer to such structures as SPT-like scar subspaces, emphasizing that the topological properties are defined at the level of the symmetry-invariant subspace rather than on a state-by-state basis. As a concrete example, we analyze the spin-$1$ Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki (AKLT) model, where a restricted spectrum-generating algebra (rSGA) generates a tower of QMBS on top of a nontrivial SPT ground state admitting a matrix product state (MPS) representation. We demonstrate that the resulting symmetry-invariant scar subspace inherits well-defined topological characteristics, encoded in bond-space symmetry representations, expectation values of symmetry-twist operators, and long-range string order in the dilute regime. We further show that these features persist in a broader class of models, including deformations and higher-spin generalizations that preserve the relevant symmetries and admit nontrivial SPT ground states with MPS representations. Our results provide a general framework in which symmetry-associated topological properties, while inherited from the ground state, are consistently realized at the level of symmetry-invariant nonthermal subspaces. This perspective clarifies how topological structures can be meaningfully defined beyond individual eigenstates.
item.dc:creator: Chihiro Matsui, Thomas Quella, Naoto Tsuji

item.title: Transversal gates for quantum CSS codes
item.description: arXiv:2601.21514v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we focus on the problem of computing the set of diagonal transversal gates fixing a CSS code. We determine the logical actions of these gates and characterize the subgroups that induce tensor products of single-qubit logical gates and logical identities. We describe these groups through explicit linear equations given by componentwise products of basis vectors of the underlying classical codes, which is the key difference from previous approaches. We compute the complete set of diagonal transversal gates fixing the code, and of transversal logical gates, for any CSS code arising from monomial codes, a family that includes decreasing monomial codes and polar codes. As a consequence, we recover and extend some results in the literature on CSS-T codes, triorthogonal codes, and divisible codes. We also extend these results to diagonal gates acting transversally on several code blocks and use them to characterize addressable gates.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Camps-Moreno, Hiram H. L\'opez, Gretchen L. Matthews, Narayanan Rengaswamy, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e

item.title: Modular Krylov Complexity as a Boundary Probe of Area Operators and Entanglement Islands
item.description: arXiv:2602.02675v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the area operator of a quantum extremal surface can be reconstructed directly from boundary dynamics without reference to bulk geometry. Our approach combines the operator-algebra quantum error-correction (OAQEC) structure of AdS/CFT with modular Krylov complexity. Using Lanczos coefficients of boundary modular dynamics, we extract the spectrum of the modular Hamiltonian restricted to the algebra of the entanglement wedge and isolate its central contribution, which is identified with the area operator. The construction is purely boundary-based and applies to superpositions of semiclassical geometries as well. As a prospective application, we discuss island formation and the Page transition in evaporating black holes using boundary modular evolution, bypassing any bulk extremization. More broadly, our results establish modular Krylov complexity as a probe of emergent spacetime geometry, providing a new route to accessing black hole interiors from boundary quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Niloofar Vardian

item.title: COACH: Toward the performance limit of traditional hybrid density functionals for molecular chemistry
item.description: arXiv:2603.23466v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) offers an exceptional balance between accuracy and efficiency, but practical density functional approximations face an unavoidable trade-off among simplicity, accuracy, and transferability. Here we present a systematic functional-development protocol that combines constraint enforcement, flexible functional forms, and modern optimization within a predefined application domain and functional class. Applying this strategy to the range-separated hybrid (RSH) meta-GGA framework, we obtain the carefully optimized and appropriately constrained hybrid (COACH) functional. Across broad molecular benchmarks, COACH improves both accuracy and transferability relative to leading RSH meta-GGAs, including \(\omega\)B97M-V, while retaining the computational practicality of its rung. These results suggest that COACH comes closer to the performance limit of traditional hybrid meta-GGA functionals for general molecular ground-state chemistry. Further substantial progress will likely require richer nonlocal or orbital-dependent information than is available from semilocal density ingredients combined with simple exact-exchange mixing.
item.dc:creator: Jiashu Liang, Martin Head-Gordon

item.title: On Sub-Sevenfold Symmetries in LH2 Stacked Ring Scaffolds: A Quantum Optical Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2603.23743v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For highly efficient light-harvesting, purple photosynthetic bacteria rely on light-harvesting 2 (LH2) complexes featuring ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold rotational symmetries; however, sub-sevenfold scaffolds have not yet been observed in nature. To investigate this absence, we utilize a closed coupled-dipole model that neglects dissipative effects, which remains valid for a temporal window shorter than the interlayer excitation energy transfer time (on the picosecond scale) in an LH2 scaffold. We examine collective eigenmodes across $C_n$ stacked model ring geometries for $n=9,8,7,6$. Our results demonstrate that the minimum energy separation between specific collective bands occurs at the angular-momentum modes $m=\pm 1$ for known geometries, effectively predicting the photoactive absorption wavelengths of the lower bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) ring. Specifically, we predict peaks at 851, 848, and 825 nm for ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold symmetries, respectively, which agree well with experimental observations. Applying this analysis to a hypothetical sixfold geometry, we predict a significant blue shift in the photoactive wavelength of the lower BChl ring, suggesting inefficient harvesting of the available solar spectrum and offering a quantum optical perspective on the evolutionary absence of sub-sevenfold scaffolds in LH2 complexes. Our study demonstrates that quantum cooperative models can elucidate specific aspects of biological LH systems.
item.dc:creator: Arpita Pal

item.title: Noise-resilient nanophotonic gyroscope with sub-prad phase resolution
item.description: arXiv:2604.00459v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optical gyroscopes based on the Sagnac effect are the cornerstone of precision orientation and navigation. However, their bulky form factors prevent deployment in emerging mobile and autonomous systems. On nanophotonic platforms, the Sagnac signal plummets under aggressive miniaturization. Consequently, the signal is easily swamped by refractive-index fluctuations, rendering navigation-grade sensitivity within just a few square millimeters a notoriously elusive goal. Here, we demonstrate a noise-resilient nanophotonic optical gyroscope by exploiting a two-chain decoupling architecture to effectively isolate the rotation signal from channel noise. Implemented on a 3 mm^2 passive silicon-nitride chip, the proof-of-concept device achieves a bias instability of 0.79 deg/h and an angle random walk of 0.0014 deg/\sqrt{h}, representing improvements of 4 and 6 orders of magnitude, respectively, over a representative nanophotonic gyroscope with the same enclosed sensing area (ref. 1). In the broader context of integrated optical gyroscopes, our approach bridges the long-standing size-performance gap by two to three orders of magnitude, moving chip-scale devices into a previously inaccessible regime and pointing toward navigation-relevant precision for monolithic microsystems. This architecture further enables an estimated input-equivalent phase resolution of 0.17 prad with general applicability, establishing a foundational framework for the next generation of robust, monolithically integrated photonic sensing systems.
item.dc:creator: Yu Tao, Xinhang Li, Jingzheng Huang, Zidi Lin, Yuyao Guo, Hongjing Li, Linjie Zhou, Guihua Zeng

item.title: Scar subspaces stabilized by algebraic closure: Beyond equally-spaced spectra and exact solvability
item.description: arXiv:2604.11015v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose algebraic closure as a stabilizing mechanism for quantum many-body scar subspaces, showing that scar states need not rely on an embedded equally spaced spectrum or analytical solvability. We formulate Lie-algebraically closed invariant subspaces and construct local quantum many-body Hamiltonians that preserve an $\mathfrak{su}(N)$-invariant scar subspace but need not act diagonally within it. Such non-diagonal action mixes the conventional tower states while preserving the multidirectional lattice-like spectral structure, allowing nonthermal dynamics and persistent multifrequency oscillations to survive even when individual scar eigenstates become analytically intractable.
item.dc:creator: Chihiro Matsui

item.title: Replica Tensor Train
item.description: arXiv:2604.22718v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a numerical many-body technique that is based on both tensor networks and quantum Monte Carlo. The variational ansatz is a tensor network that can harvest volume-law entanglement. It is constructed from a tensor train to which one applies a set of non-local operators that force several indices of the tensor train to represent the same physical index, hence its name -- replica tensor train (RTT). From the tensor network toolbox, it inherits the possibility to make linear combinations of these states and apply a certain class of operators. We can therefore find the ground-state of a local Hamiltonian in a purely algebraic way as in standard tensor network algorithms -- i.e. without using gradient descent methods. On the other hand, the volume-law structure forbids calculating physical observables directly. In much the same way as on a quantum computer where one can prepare a state but can only sample it at the end, here we have to use Markov Chain Monte Carlo to compute the observables. We further show that the approach can be extended to build Krylov-subspace ground-state methods within the variational manifold. We illustrate the different algorithms on a two-dimensional spin model with a transverse magnetic field, which can be solved by this approach at low computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Miha Srdinsek, Gabriel Gouraud, Xavier Waintal

item.title: Bayesian phase transition for the critical Ising model: Enlarged replica symmetry in the epsilon expansion and in 2D
item.description: arXiv:2604.23346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A process that images or measures bond energies in the critical Ising model can be in distinct measurement 'phases', depending on the precision of measurement. We study the transition into the strong-measurement phase using replica field theory (an epsilon expansion around six dimensions), a symmetry analysis, and numerical simulations in two dimensions. The results show that certain inference problems possess unexpected structure associated with an enlarged symmetry of the replica description. The symmetry imposes constraints on correlation functions, and is an analog of the Nishimori phenomenon in the Ising spin glass, but in a distinct replica limit. It determines the exact critical exponent for an Edwards-Anderson-like correlator in the measured Ising model, both in 2D and near the upper critical dimension. The symmetry is present microscopically for certain measurement protocols, and it emerges in the infrared for generic protocols at the critical measurement strength. We also examine the epsilon expansion for models with power-law interactions and/or long-range measurement. Finally, we describe an analogous replica symmetry enlargement for measurement in Wegner's lattice gauge theory.
item.dc:creator: Kay Joerg Wiese, Alapan Das, Adam Nahum

item.title: Constructing Bulk Topological Orders via Layered Gauging
item.description: arXiv:2604.27363v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding quantum phases and phase transitions in the presence of symmetries is a central objective of quantum many-body physics. A powerful modern paradigm for investigating this problem is topological holography, which relates symmetries in $k$ dimensions to "bulk" topological orders in $(k+1)$ dimensions. While conceptually profound, most existing bulk construction methods rely on sophisticated mathematical formalisms and can be difficult to apply to certain symmetry types. In this work, we propose a physically intuitive and versatile method, termed the layered gauging construction, to systematically generate $(k+1)$-dimensional (liquid or fracton) topological orders from $k$-dimensional generalized symmetries. Roughly speaking, the prescription is to stack many layers of $k$-dimensional quantum systems with certain symmetries into a $(k+1)$-dimensional pile, and then sequentially gauge a diagonal symmetry acting on each nearest-neighbor pair of layers. The detailed procedure depends on the specific symmetry types. We have successfully implemented the method in a number of examples in different spatial dimensions, with symmetries that are conventional, higher-form, subsystem, anomalous, nonabelian, or noninvertible. We hence conjecture the method to be very general. For example, from the subsystem symmetry of the $2d$ plaquette Ising model, we derive the X-cube model and also an anisotropic fracton topological order. Additionally, starting from an anomalous $Z_2$ symmetry in $1d$, we construct a new square lattice model realizing the double semion topological order. From a quantum-error-correction perspective, our layered gauging construction may be viewed as a generalization of the hypergraph-product construction beyond the standard Calderbank-Shor-Steane setting.
item.dc:creator: Shang Liu

item.title: The Quantum Noise Fraction and the addressable fraction in High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection
item.description: arXiv:2605.00053v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quantum noise fraction $\beta$, the share of a detector's noise power that is quantum in origin, sets a ceiling $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 1/\sqrt{1-\beta}$ on the sensitivity improvement that removing quantum-origin noise can yield. In the kHz--GHz band the readout degree of freedom is a bosonic mode and $\beta = 1/(2\bar{n}_{\mathrm{th}}+1)$, with $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{th}}$ the Bose--Einstein occupation. Quantum noise then dominates only on the cold side of the thermal frontier $k_BT\ln 3 = \hbar\omega$ (above 229 MHz at 10 mK), which governs mechanical resonators and electromagnetic cavities alike; a real readout turns it into a joint condition on the occupation and on the excess noise of the readout chain. On a multimode acoustic antenna the frontier can be observed within one device, since the logarithmic slope of $\sqrt{S_hQ}$ along the odd-overtone comb increases by one half across it whatever the dependence of the quality factor on overtone number. On this antenna, crossing the frontier costs more in classical sensitivity than quantum enhancement returns. For a GHz mode of an existing bulk acoustic wave device at 10 mK, $\beta = 0.984$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 7.8$. That ceiling cannot be reached with a linear readout, because with intrinsic damping the zero-point term is the force noise of the bath, fixed by the fluctuation--dissipation theorem. The addressable fraction $\beta_a$ excludes it: at the standard quantum limit the same mode has $\beta = 0.992$ but $\beta_a = 0.496$, an available improvement of 1.41 against a ceiling of 11.0. An array of $10^4$ such devices cross-correlated for one year reaches $3.6\times 10^{-24}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ for an integration bandwidth equal to the linewidth; even granting $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{max}} = 7.8$ in full, a factor $1.0\times 10^{10}$ above the big-bang-nucleosynthesis bound remains, and it is classical.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Gaudio

item.title: Computing eigenpairs of quantum many-body systems with Polfed.jl
item.description: arXiv:2605.10191v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present Polfed$.$jl, an open-source Julia package implementing the Polynomially Filtered Exact Diagonalization (POLFED) algorithm for computing mid-spectrum eigenvalues and eigenvectors (shortly, eigenpairs) of quantum many-body Hamiltonians. Access to such eigenpairs is essential for studying non-equilibrium many-body physics, but is hindered by the exponential growth of Hilbert-space dimension. POLFED addresses this challenge through a polynomial spectral transformation evaluated on the fly within a Lanczos iteration, preserving Hamiltonian sparsity and substantially reducing memory costs compared to other diagonalization methods. The package supports flexible energy targeting, automatic optimization of the spectral mapping for structured Hamiltonians, and GPU acceleration, which is particularly effective since the dominant computational cost reduces to repeated sparse matrix-vector multiplications. Benchmarks on disordered spin-chain and fermionic models demonstrate access to larger system sizes than alternative approaches, and CPU--GPU comparisons confirm significant speedups. In particular, we also provide code for constructing the quantum sun model Hamiltonian, a toy model of a many-body ergodicity-breaking transition. While our focus is on many-body Hamiltonians, Polfed$.$jl may be applied to any large sparse matrix.
item.dc:creator: Rok Pintar, Konrad Pawlik, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Miroslav Hopjan, Jan \v{S}untajs, Jakub Zakrzewski, Piotr Sierant, Lev Vidmar

item.title: QPipe: LLM-Based Agentic Quantum Application Generation for Test Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.00939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum computing is increasingly explored for software engineering (SE) optimization, but translating natural-language (NL) task-level requirements into executable quantum applications still demands substantial quantum and programming expertise. We present QPipe, a large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent architecture that autonomously turns NL requirements into traceable quantum-application workflows through specialized agents for requirement parsing, formulation, code generation, review, execution, and verification. We evaluate QPipe on 20 NL requirements, each associated with a real-world benchmark and a test-optimization problem. QPipe successfully completes the key stages of quantum-application generation across requirements, achieving average rates of 100% for code compilation and 96.7% for application execution and final-result combination, with average generation costs of 260.1 seconds and 1.89M tokens per requirement. Among the generated quantum applications that execute successfully, the returned solutions outperform the offline genetic algorithm baseline in most cases. Ablation results further show that QPipe's advantage depends on retaining code-generation skills, task knowledge, review feedback, and multi-agent decomposition. These results indicate that agentic coordination can support generation of executable quantum applications for tackling test optimization problems from real-world benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Ming Tao, Yuechen Li, Tao Yue, Man Zhang, Aitor Arrieta Marcos

item.title: Entanglement asymmetry in the gapped XYZ spin-$\frac12$ chain
item.description: arXiv:2607.25625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The entanglement asymmetry measures how strongly a symmetry is broken inside a subsystem. Analytic results at equilibrium have so far covered free theories and, perturbatively, the critical XXZ chain. We compute the R\'enyi entanglement asymmetries of a large interval in the gapped, $U(1)$-breaking phase of the interacting XYZ chain. The calculation combines three ingredients. A charged-moment identity, which we prove for fermionic Gaussian and for injective matrix-product ground states, ties the asymmetry to the static susceptibility of the broken charge. A non-conservation sum rule then evaluates the susceptibility from sine-Gordon form factors, its two-kink and one-breather channels providing a lower bound on the universal amplitude. The Baxter--Johnson--Krinsky--McCoy solution supplies the kink mass for different couplings. Infinite-system density-matrix renormalization group simulations built on these masses reproduce the master formula.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Taha Sant'Ana

item.title: Matrix Holography on an Optical Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2609.05613v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose an analog quantum-simulation protocol based on a lattice of atomic ensembles and time-averaged Floquet dynamics to construct the four-body potentials that typically appear in bosonic BFSS-like matrix quantum mechanics. In contrast to gate-based digital implementations requiring deep circuits, our approach generates the target model through a fixed set of control stages per Floquet cycle, keeping the number of consecutive unitaries constant with respect to the matrix size $N$. The principal scaling cost in our construction is given by the frequency range required to control the growing lattice. We show that this cost grows at most as $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$, giving a polynomial scaling route to large$-N$, attractive to experimental implementation. Additionally, we demonstrate that the coupling parameter can be tuned beyond $\mathcal{O}(1)$, enabling the simulation of strong-coupling physics necessary for holographic phases.
item.dc:creator: Robin L\"owenberg, Julian Sonner

item.title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
item.description: arXiv:2609.20597v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L$. Thus $\lambda_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Loy, Jan C. Louw

item.title: Effective atom-dimer bands of three-body lattice systems at strong coupling: exact critical mass ratios and a statistics-quasimomentum duality
item.description: arXiv:2609.33576v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study three particles on the two-dimensional square lattice with contact interactions of infinite strength, in every sector of total quasimomentum, for three statistics: identical bosons, two identical fermions with a distinguishable third particle, and two identical bosons with a distinguishable third particle. The atom-dimer sector associated with the infinitely degenerate eigenvalue of the pair-contact operator is analysed on the whole Brillouin zone. A Feshbach-Schur reduction gives explicit effective Hamiltonians built from the Dirichlet Laplacian and a rank-four exchange operator, and a spectral transfer theorem with explicit error bounds identifies the atom-dimer threshold of the three-body operator with that of the effective one; the eigenvalue counting function below the threshold is squeezed between those of the effective operator, so that the number of atom-dimer states bound uniformly in the coupling equals the number of bound states of the effective Hamiltonian. The threshold problem reduces to a four-by-four Hermitian matrix whose zero-energy limit is built from the two-point resistances of the square lattice and hence to a quartic polynomial. This yields the complete atom-dimer zones in closed form; the critical hopping ratio as an explicit function on the whole Brillouin zone with two-sided bounds and closed forms at all symmetry points; at most two atom-dimer states per sector with an explicit second threshold; exact onset laws of infinite order at the corner point and linear-over-logarithmic in the pure p-wave channel; and two exact dualities relating a change of statistics to a shift of quasimomentum by half a reciprocal-lattice vector. The reduction of the three-body eigenvalue problem to the lattice Skornyakov-Ter-Martirosyan equation is proved with an explicit isomorphism of eigenspaces.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail V. Dolgopolov

item.title: Quantum Simulation of Detuning-Controlled Proximity-Induced Localization and Reentrant Delocalization in a Quasiperiodic Ladder
item.description: arXiv:2609.37059v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Proximity effects, in which one subsystem imprints its properties onto another, offer a route to controlling quantum matter. For localization, this raises the question of whether an extended system can be localized by its neighbor, and then delocalized again, in the regime of weak quasiperiodic disorder. Here, we demonstrate this behavior in a coupled Aubry--Andr\'e ladder, where a staggered detuning applied to only one leg localizes the neighboring, undetuned leg through inter-leg hybridization, even before the detuned leg itself localizes. Upon further increasing the detuning, the undetuned leg undergoes re-entrant delocalization, while the detuned leg remains localized. Finite-size scaling supports the persistence of these regimes in the thermodynamic limit. On an IBM Quantum processor, we experimentally observe their dynamical signatures: strongly suppressed wave-packet spreading in the proximity-localized regime and its recovery upon re-entrant delocalization. Our results establish leg-selective detuning as a reversible control knob for localization and transport in coupled quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Mrinal Kanti Giri, Shih Tai-Ming, Pinaki Sengupta, Pochung Chen

item.title: A Quantum Scaling Algorithm for Maximum-Weight Perfect Matching in General Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.39457v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum speed-ups have been obtained for many fundamental graph problems, including most variants of matching. A notable exception, however, is the maximum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) problem in general graphs with integer edge weights, which is arguably the most challenging variant of matching. We present a quantum algorithm for MWPM in general graphs that runs in $\widetilde{O}(n m^{2/3}\log W)$ time, where $W$ is an upper bound on the magnitude of the edge weights. This is an improvement over the best known classical combinatorial bound of $\widetilde{O}(m\sqrt n \log W)$ in the dense regime, where $m\ge n^{3/2}$. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first quantum algorithm to obtain an asymptotic improvement over the best classical combinatorial algorithm for the MWPM problem in general graphs. The running time of our method accounts for QRAM initialization and access overheads up to polylogarithmic factors, as well as all classical updates to the data structures. At a high level, our algorithm is based on a classical framework due to Duan, Pettie, and Su, but our algorithm requires replacing certain classical tasks with quantum methods, alternative analysis of classical procedures, and the use of alternative data structures that can be implemented effectively in the QRAM model.
item.dc:creator: Kourosh Mirsohi, Sandy Irani, Michael T. Goodrich

item.title: Smooth perturbation theory and generic Cantor spectrum for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.00733v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider multi-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators with monotone sawtooth-type potentials in the perturbative localization regime. We prove that a given gap is closed iff a corresponding (via a natural gap labeling) eigenfunction vanishes at the origin. Using this, we show that for a generic choice of the sampling function $f$, the spectrum of such an operator is a Cantor set, with all possible gaps being open. We also provide a class of functions $f$ for which some gaps are closed. Finally, we observe that certain gaps are more difficult to close than the others.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Kachkovskiy, Leonid Parnovski, Roman Shterenberg

item.title: Arithmetic of qudit dimensions governs erasure correction on the Fano plane and stabilizer-state entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2610.18905v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Qudit codes often inherit the parameters of qubit codes, but not necessarily their correctable erasures. We show that a code encoding one qudit of dimension D into seven such qudits that corrects every erasure Steane's code corrects exists exactly when D is a power of 2; for the qutrit color code, exactly when D is odd. This needs no stabilizer assumption: these codes are, up to local unitaries, stabilizer codes of qubits, respectively prime-power qudits. The two patterns differ in one line, which completes the Fano plane only where 1+1=0. As ideal secret sharing schemes, these codes exist exactly where classical ones do: entanglement does not help, unlike for Euler's 36 officers. The same arithmetic makes the entropy cones of qubit and odd-dimensional stabilizer states incomparable from six parties on. At five, the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, answering an open question.
item.dc:creator: Xidan Song, Ruifeng Cao

item.title: Fractal Period Locking and Action-Quantized Resonances in the Open Quantum Baker Map
item.description: arXiv:2610.23573v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We open the quantum baker map with a position window of width $w$ and center $q_c$. Classical pruning tiles the $(q_c,w)$ plane into diamonds where the $T$ leading resonances form root-of-unity multiplets. At $w=1/2$ one periodic orbit survives for almost every $q_c$, and the multiplets are quantized without free parameters: their modulus $2^{-1/2}$ saturates the pressure bound and their phase is the orbit action. The multiplets form cycling multicomponent cat states. Finally, the opening reduces to one flag qubit per step, and on an IBM superconducting processor the return probability already revives at the period selected by the window.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Ermann

item.title: Moments of Random Permanents and Hafnians: A Replica Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.27872v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using contour-integral representations of the permanent and of the Hafnian, we turn the computation of their moments for random matrices into a replica calculation, analogous to that of the moments of the partition function of a mean-field spin glass. For the $2k$-th moment of $N\times N$ matrices with independent entries, the dominant saddle point is replica symmetric for $k>2$, and we obtain in closed form the exponential growth rate, the prefactor and the first $1/N$ correction, in agreement with exact enumerations. The growth rate depends only on whether the entries are real or complex; higher cumulants affect only the prefactor and the $1/N$ term. At $k=2$ the replica-symmetric solution becomes unstable, separating a power-law bulk of the distribution from a large-deviation tail, which we compute. The results apply to boson sampling with single photons and with squeezed light.

item.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.32973v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defects and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincar\'e variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincar\'e method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection. Suitable variational regularizations are also proposed to deal with the motion of singular defect lines.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Gay-Balmaz, Tudor S. Ratiu, Cesare Tronci

item.title: Deep-Microscopic Photonic Bandstructure of a Two-Dimensional Honeycomb Lattice
item.description: arXiv:2610.33709v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conventional descriptions of light in materials rely on macroscopic models that average the optical response over the microscopic lattice structures. These models are deployed in the semi-classical limit, where the collective local response over many lattice sites is adequate. However, they fail to capture the full spatial dispersion, which requires a lattice-resolved description of light. We address this limitation by formulating a deep-microscopic nonlocal theory of the photon based on the Maxwell Hamiltonian and its characteristic equation. The solution reveals the full spatial dispersion in the form of deep-microscopic photonic bandstructure, and corresponding real-space Bloch field textures. We demonstrate our theory for a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model of a gapped honeycomb lattice. Our framework thus extends photons to the same microscopic footing as electrons or phonons, providing a unified route to studying topology, dissipation, and quantum fluctuations of light in dispersive materials.
item.dc:creator: Pronoy Das, Sathwik Bharadwaj, Wenbo Sun, Zubin Jacob

item.title: Symmetry-resolved quasilocal entanglement as a key to Mott and pseudogap physics in plaquette CDMFT
item.description: arXiv:2610.34470v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In order to identify intrinsic quantum resources in strongly interacting fermionic systems, we introduce a symmetry resolution of the parity-superselected two-site entanglement, as measured by both the fermionic negativity and the relative entropy of entanglement. We discuss how the symmetry resolution can be extended also to the full entanglement in pure and mixed two-site states. We apply our recipe to the Hubbard model, first for a dimer, and then for a plaquette cluster dynamical mean-field theory, an established method tailored to accurately capture short-range correlations. Following the evolution of the model through the interaction- and density-driven Mott transitions at zero temperature, we highlight how the three symmetry-resolved components of the two-site entanglement probe different key aspects of Mott and pseudogap physics.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Bellomia, Carlos Mejuto-Zaera, Massimo Capone, Adriano Amaricci

item.title: Kelvin-Wave Multiplication by Sound Emission
item.description: arXiv:2610.39909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kelvin waves are bending excitations of a quantized vortex. We identify a subsonic decay channel in which one Kelvin quantum emits a phonon and splits into two lower-energy Kelvin quanta, reducing the Kelvin-wave energy while increasing the number of quanta. For sound wavelengths much longer than the Kelvin wavelengths, rotational symmetry fixes the leading shear contribution to the emission amplitude in terms of the released Kelvin energy. This contribution is odd in the phonon momentum along the vortex. Microscopic calculations support the relation. Coherently seeded Gross--Pitaevskii evolution in a reflecting cavity demonstrates phase-controlled Kelvin gain, with increased mean-square vortex displacement and reduced mean-square slope.
item.dc:creator: Weican Yang

item.title: Characteristics of VHF and UHF band detection using Stark shifting in Rydberg-atom sensors
item.description: arXiv:2610.40952v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a characterization of the sensitivity of broadband electric field measurements in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands using AC stark shifting of Rydberg states. The dependence of the sensitivity and dynamic range of the field measurements using nD5/2 states of cesium for principal quantum numbers n= 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 is presented, detailing the intricacies involved. The frequencies considered for the measurement range from 50 MHz to 900 MHz for which a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is used to excite the Rydberg atoms with the RF fields. The relative sensitivities achieved for various principal quantum numbers are presented. A general trend of better sensitivity for higher principal quantum numbers is observed. This work paves the way for a better understanding of the AC Stark dependent field measurements using Rydberg sensors.
item.dc:creator: Rajavardhan Talashila, Noah Schlossberger, David S. La Mantia, Abby Halasi-Kun, Baran Kayim, Michael A. Viray, Robert Wyllie, Christopher L. Holloway, Nikunjkumar Prajapati
